newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Rebel faction vows neutrality in Cambodia rift.
newsitem.headline: Rebel faction vows neutrality in Cambodia rift.

text.p: A dissident Khmer Rouge guerrilla faction which defected to the government side last year said it planned to stay neutral over a rift in the Cambodian ruling coalition.
"Our elder leader has repeatedly said that we will be strictly neutral in the conflict in the coalition government," General Ie Chian, commander of the Pailin division, told Reuters over the weekend.
"Elder leader" referred to Ieng Sary, who was foreign minister during the Khmer Rouge's reign of terror when it held power in the 1970s.
Last August Ieng Sary led about 4,000 guerrillas from the Phnom Malai and Pailin regions in western Cambodia in a break from hardliners in the Maoist group led by Pol Pot.

They defected to the Cambodian government, which has been riven by a feud between First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh of the royalist Funcinpec party and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen of the Cambodian Peoples Party.
Chian, who was promoted to the rank of full general in the government's armed forces, said siding with Hun Sen or Ranarridh could bring on civil war.
"If we were to side with one party it would be like putting fuel on the fire," Chian added.
Analysts have said the support of Khmer Rouge defectors could tip the balance in the rivalry between the two ruling parties, which jointly rule the country in an uneasy alliance.
Verbal sparring between Ranariddh and Hun Sen, which stems partly from their efforts to draw support ahead of national polls next year, has heightened over the last few months.
Since the Khmer Rouge defections in August, both Hun Sen and Ranariddh have each sought to woo the former guerrillas, offering various concessions.
They have allowed them relatively free rein in their power base, the gem-rich region of Pailin, which has been prospering since the breakaway.
The Khmer Rouge signed a U.N. sponsored peace pact in 1991 but later reneged on the deal and have been fighting the government which Ranariddh and Hun Sen formed after a 1993 general election.
